previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a complex history including end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease with prior CABG and stents, peripheral vascular disease, and type 2 diabetes was admitted for sudden-onset chest tightness associated with nausea and vomiting. The pain began at home and recurred during a dialysis session, prompting ER evaluation. Initial troponin levels were stable, and a nuclear stress test showed no reversible ischemia, indicating no acute coronary event. Management focused on optimizing anti-anginal therapy, including increasing metoprolol and switching from isosorbide dinitrate to once-daily isosorbide mononitrate. Fluid overload was noted on chest imaging and managed with dialysis. The patient also received podiatry care for chronic lower extremity ulcers. He remained stable, pain-free, and was discharged home with medication changes, weight monitoring instructions, and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr ___ was admitted for chest pain.  His troponins were 
stable 0.09 - 0.11.  His EKG did show T wave inversions 
progressively deepening in lead I and aVL; enzymes however did 
not increase.  We felt his EKG changes were most likely 
secondary to anginal pain.  He was given nitroglycerin with some 
relief along with morphine.  To treat his anginal pain, we also 
increased his Imdur dose.  We observed him on telemetry and 
serial EKGs revealed no worsening changes.  He underwent HD on 
day 2 of his hospitalization per his HD schedule and had no 
events during or after HD.  He was chest-pain free on the higher 
dose of Imdur at time of discharge; we otherwise continued his 
home regimen.  We discharged him with cardiology follow-up.
